title: Conjunctions
definition: Conjunctions connect words, phrases, or clauses. Common A1 conjunctions such as und, aber, oder, and denn keep normal verb-second order in the following main clause. Weil introduces a subordinate clause, where the conjugated verb goes to the end.

rules.title: und — and
rules.explanation: Adds information. The clause after und normally keeps the standard main-clause word order.

examples.german: Ich lerne Deutsch und mein Bruder lernt Englisch.
examples.english: I learn German and my brother learns English.

rules.title: aber — but
rules.explanation: Shows contrast; the conjugated verb remains in position two.

examples.german: Ich bin müde, aber ich gehe zur Arbeit.
examples.english: I am tired, but I am going to work.
Would you like tea or coffee?

rules.title: denn — because / for
rules.explanation: Gives a reason and keeps the normal main-clause word order.

examples.german: Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn ich bin krank.
examples.english: I am staying at home because I am ill.

rules.title: weil — because
rules.explanation: Weil introduces a subordinate clause. The conjugated verb goes to the end of that clause.

examples.german: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
examples.english: I am staying at home because I am ill.

examples.german: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland wohne.
examples.english: I am learning German because I live in Germany.

rules.title: deshalb — therefore / that's why
rules.explanation: Deshalb is an adverb, not a conjunction like und. If it begins the clause, the conjugated verb comes next.

examples.german: Ich bin krank. Deshalb bleibe ich zu Hause.
examples.english: I am ill. Therefore, I am staying at home.

common_mistakes.wrong: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich bin krank.
common_mistakes.correct: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
common_mistakes.explanation: The conjugated verb goes to the end after weil.
Deshalb occupies the first position, so the verb follows it.

mastery_goal: You can connect simple ideas using common conjunctions and keep the correct verb position.
